title: White Rice with Carrots, Dark Green Vegetables and Tomato‑Based Sauce, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled white rice stir‑fried with carrots, dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach) and a tomato‑based sauce, to which a small amount of oil or butter has been added for flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is a staple carbohydrate source for many cultures worldwide.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables contain chlorophyll and high levels of B‑vitamins.
Tomato sauce provides lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health.
Adding a little fat helps absorb the fat‑soluble vitamins from the vegetables.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice supplies quick‑acting complex carbohydrates for sustained energy.

items.title: Vitamin A from carrots
items.content: Beta‑carotene supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Antioxidants from tomatoes
items.content: Lycopene protects cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Phytonutrients from dark green veg
items.content: Chlorophyll, folate, and vitamin K promote healthy blood and bones.

items.title: Improved nutrient absorption
items.content: Fat aids the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) found in the vegetables.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt, which may affect blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Fat intolerance
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to certain fats, such as butter.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Using non‑organic vegetables may leave pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or as a side to meat, fish, or legumes. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, basil) for extra aroma. You can increase the vegetable proportion or swap the added fat for olive oil if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or broth to restore moisture.
